title: CodeChallenge: Cosine similarity in word sequences

cues.en: In the previous video, we focused on cosine similarity between pairs of tokens, but those tokens had no sequence to them.
cues.zh: 上一支看詞元配對的餘弦，但沒有序列。

cues.en: In real language communication, words are meaningful when they are put into a sequence to form sentences and discourse.
cues.zh: 真實溝通中，字詞排成句子、篇章，才有意義。

cues.en: And so what we are going to do in this code challenge is investigate how to use cosine similarity when exploring word sequences.
cues.zh: 這個挑戰，就用餘弦探索字詞序列。

cues.en: Now the thing is that cosine similarity is still just a bivariate statistic.
cues.zh: 但它仍只是雙變量統計。

cues.en: So it doesn't matter how many tokens there are in a sequence, we can only calculate cosine similarity between two token embeddings vectors at a time.
cues.zh: 序列不管多長，一次只能算兩個詞元嵌入向量。

cues.en: So what we are going to do is form sentences and then calculate cosine similarity between successive pairs of token embedding vectors.
cues.zh: 所以，先組句子，再算相鄰配對的餘弦。

cues.en: It's actually fairly straightforward, and it will set us up for similar kinds of analyses that will apply to deeper layers in the LMS in later sections.
cues.zh: 很直接，也為後面 LLM 深層的類似分析鋪路。

cues.en: Okay.
And we will use the Bert embeddings and tokenizer for this code challenge.
cues.zh: 這次用 BERT 嵌入與 tokenizer。

cues.en: So I suppose exercise zero would be to just import the Bert data.
cues.zh: 所以練習零，就是匯入資料。

cues.en: Okay.
Here is the main goal of exercise one.
Here is a sentence down here.
My phone is in the kitchen near the cold ice cream.
cues.zh: 「我的手機在廚房，靠近冰冷的冰淇淋。」

cues.en: What you see plotted here is cosine similarity of each sequential pair of token embeddings.
cues.zh: 圖上是每對相鄰詞元嵌入的餘弦。

cues.en: So my is the first word and there's no word before it.
cues.zh: my 是第一字，前面沒有字，

cues.en: So there's no cosine similarity.
The second token in this sentence is phone.
So this value over here is 0.19 or whatever.
And this is the cosine similarity between the embedding for phone and the embedding vector for my.
cues.zh: 是 phone 與 my 向量的相似度。

cues.en: And then this value over here is the cosine similarity between is and phone and so on all the way up until the end of the sequence.
cues.zh: 接著是 is 與 phone，依此直到結尾。

cues.en: So this value here is cosine similarity between cream and ice.
I hope you enjoy working through this exercise.
The next two exercises are fairly similar to this one.
So if you solve this one meticulously then the next two will be easier.
cues.zh: 這題仔細解，後面更容易。

Just importing some stuff and extracting some stuff.
Okay.
And here we get to exercise one.

Don't forget that Bert will always add these special tokens at the beginning and at the end of a text.

cues.en: Okay, so here I am initializing the cosine similarity vector.
I call this vector cos sim.

That means that in lots of texts that Bert has digested and trained on, it doesn't often see the word

These are very similar words.
They often appear together.
They are semantically related to each other.
So ice is going to have a strong cosine similarity to cold.
cues.zh: 所以 ice 與 cold 餘弦高。

cues.zh: cream 與 ice 也一樣。

So you know we could also expect a reasonable cosine similarity between those two words, but that is not present in this particular analysis.
cues.zh: 也可能合理地預期這兩字相似，但這分析沒算。

cues.en: Of course, you can do that if you want, but this is only showing the cosine similarities between each word and the previous word.
cues.zh: 想做可以，這裡只顯示每字與前字。

cues.en: Consider the following two sentences.
The conductor waved his hands as the train departed, and the conductor waved his hands as the orchestra began.
cues.zh: 「The conductor waved his hands as the train departed」，以及「The conductor waved his hands as the orchestra began」。

cues.en: Now these two sentences are exactly identical up until the penultimate word.
cues.zh: 兩句直到倒數第二字前，都完全相同。

cues.en: So what does your brain do when it first reads or hears the word conductor?
cues.zh: 首次讀、聽到 conductor，腦做什麼？

cues.en: Well, your brain's language centers have to remain open to some amount of ambiguity and flexibility
cues.zh: 語言中心必須保留一些模糊、彈性，

cues.en: because the word conductor has multiple meanings depending on the context.
cues.zh: 因為 conductor 隨語境，可指列車員或指揮等。

cues.en: It's only when you get to the end of the sentence that you can reinterpret this word conductor.
cues.zh: 到句尾，才能重新解讀它。

cues.en: So it's an interesting question of how the brain solves this problem.
But that's not what we are going to work on here.
We are going to discuss whether an embeddings matrix can deal with this ambiguity and reinterpretation of this word conductor.
cues.zh: 要談嵌入矩陣能否處理這種歧義、重新解讀。

cues.zh: 但先提個統計視覺化細節：嚴格、正式地說，不應該用線連起
